items.title: [负面] I want to start by saying this is by far one of th...
items.summary:
I want to start by saying this is by far one of the best games I've played in terms of gameplay, and I specifically liked one gamemode that heavily incentivized team creativity.

That gamemode, has just been utterly destroyed to the core. The easiest difficulty compared to the second easiest has a difference of 10x HP which makes just thinking about playing the game a slog. Previously we had 5 Difficulties and now they've been compressed into 2, with it being arguably harder, including the really bad gimmicks implemented on the final boss. This also came with 2 higher difficulties to appease the whales, which changed absolutely nothing because its just about 9 times the HP of the second easiest difficulty. We were also given the ability to use revives, which we previously couldn't, and it was stated that this would not change the difficulty. And it absolutely did.

This has also come with some questionable changes done to units, all under the guise of a "bug fix", and such mechanics were stablished for long gone (and for the most recent, since release, more than a year ago). What makes it even more dubious is the fact that the unit and the weapon interaction that were changed had just reran back to back, with some people spending tons to maximize this BiS combination.

Its been less than 3 days with no response, which would be fair if the gamemode change wasn't as monumental as it was, making many players uninvested to even want to touch it anymore. 

Back when I joined, there was a very clear future that seemed promising to me. Now? I wouldn't be surprised if it were to be announced to EoS.

Lastly, as just my tiny teensie bit of fustration with the changes, 

"Unplayable" doesn't begin to describe this update, this game rewards pure whaling and nothing else, I am beyond convinced at this point. After waiting hours and hours for the dtide, having to do change my schedule just to fit in my very thin slice of time to play this rotation, attempting hard mode somehow felt even worse than I had thought possible. My team was superior, my relics were superior, my play was superior, and I lost. I don't see a reason to continue engaging in an activity where what is within my control is overwhelmingly outweighed by what is not.

I am done with D-Tide, and you won't get a fond farewell. This rotation is infected to its roots with a degenerative disease that grows stronger over time but stops short of killing its host. Alert 5 used to have a competitive spirit at its heart, this has been transplanted and replaced with an artificial organ that feeds numbers and numbers from fodder mobs that rips appart teams over the pretense of "making the game better". The enviroment we fostered has trapped us all like this in a vicious cycle, and escaping it requires acceptance of the harshest reality we all scramble to explain away, that none of the countless straining efforts we put ourselves through to give feedback will ever amount to one single shining glimmer of a response. I would make this the end, but Arc 2 is still ongoing, and I would never leave so many great friends out dry, so I'll suffer through a few more rotations for them.

One last thing before I leave you all to react with disdain, ridicule, and self-righteous ferver, before you do everything in your power to minimize my words and thoughts, box them up and shove them to some cobwebbed corner of your memory, and hope they disappear forever as a stain on your finite time ground to dust. From this moment on, none of your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gimmicks matter to me. The foulest number bloats, fervor, full immunity, shield ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, with intent to make the game "fun" will calmly settle at the earth before my feet, and the dissolute like a warm summer breeze. This game is less than anything conceivable, while I carry on, brimming with joy distilled from detachment.

items.title: [负面] I absolutely love Morimens, and a few months ago I...
items.summary:
I absolutely love Morimens, and a few months ago I would undoubtedly give the game a positive review. Infact, if the general issues with the games are resolved I will swap my review to positive right away. However, a recent change in management has brought with it a myriad of problems. Instead of the specifics of every horrible patch, I will explain the general trend. In short, the game has been shifting away from openly communicating with and rewarding its community by introducing baffling decision after baffling decision that is causing the most extreme alienation of the player base to date. 

Historically, the developers have been open to feedback and open in discussing their plans. However, lately the communication has been abysmal, with blatant lies regarding viability of certain units/teams and abrupt changes to mechanics right after players have invested large amounts of resources just to learn all their money spent has been rendered essentially worthless in endgame content.

Without delving into the mountain of issues that have been building up patch after patch, it is clear to everyone that the major problem is not just the changes themselves, but the way the developers announce a change, backtrack on the change within a day, THEN BACKTRACK ON THE BACKTRACKING! There is no transparency as to why health numbers are massively inflated by 10x what was promised, or why the new affinity rework is extremely time consuming and unrewarding, or why a known interaction in the game was nerfed after 1.5 years, specifically RIGHT after both the Unit and Wheel involved in the interaction ran FOR MULTIPLE WEEKS!

Everyone understands that a game needs to make money to succeed, and that money must come from somewhere. The game already requires 15(!!) copies to max out a unit, but most content use to be clearable by a dedicated and creative player with the free resources provided (though this requires a lot of knowledge of the meta, since investing too much in the wrong units can brick your account, which is a whole nother issue...). Even still, people do not have an issue with all the ways the game tries to make money, and people understand there is a lot of content designed for whales. Even changes such as buffing +12 units is not something universally disliked. But at the end of the day, everything requires transparency. If you claim to listen to community feedback, why would you lie to their face about thoroughly testing the new changes to endgame content? They claimed to have tested poison and counter on the new mode, when the cap for poison and counter is less than 1/100th of the boss' health!

There is still a lot of good! The game has been great for over 2 years and has built an amazing foundation that tests creativity in teambuilding and gameplay. However, everything that has occurred in the last few months have been a sign that new management does not care about openness, but instead just about squeezing every cent out of player's investment just to pivot with no warning to force everyone to once again open their wallet. I sincerely wish for nothing but the best from this game, but it is mindboggling just how many times the developers have shot themselves in the foot for no reason other than greed. I hope that the people involved in making these decisions listen to the community and reflect on why everyone is angry, and understand that this new business model cannot last.

items.title: [负面] This may unironically be a top 3 worst patches a g...
items.summary:
This may unironically be a top 3 worst patches a gacha has ever made that didn't directly go after pull rates or mass nerf characters. I don't particularly care if it's dev greed, investor greed, "helpful suggestions" from their Japanses partners, or Light's literal brain parasites when it comes to poor game balance philosophy, because the fact this happened to this extent means I really can never recommend this game again.

- Made the already most whale-heavy equipment (covenants) more expensive by creating a system where you now must make a unique set for every character to get their full stats
- Nerfed affinity gain while adding a prohibitively overcosted item to extend further. (couldn't just let people have the pulls from raising affinity, I guess?)
- Made the standard currency shop far more expensive
- Hideous amounts of stat bloat in both story and repeatable content
- """Bugfixed""" an interaction that had existed for over a year, nerfing a character in the process (the character had rerun a matter of weeks prior, and the equipment they interacted with is running *now* and had been running for 2 weeks prior to the bugfix, so it was clearly timed to get pulls before nerfing it. The character isn't even particularly strong. this is the third time they've done this under the guise of a bugfix.
- Probably the most abrasively designed boss the game has ever seen
- Ruined the one gamemode for low/mid-investment players to come around and play semifrequently, making it prohibitively difficult, far too overbearingly scaled between difficulty levels (Minor team improvements matter in basically no content now) and balanced the higher tiers around E3+12 characters (YOU HAVE TO PULL SIXTEEN COPIES OF A CHARACTER TO GET THEIR +12 TALENT) and even then 80% of characters straight up feel unviable in a game with ~60 characters where you need 19-20 to get a clear, and 39-40 to max out potential gains in this mode. There is no middle investment anymore.
- Also there's frequent lag spikes now
- I am almost certainly missing other issues.

Shame that a game where you used to be able to get by by playing exceptionally well has added such nasty stat checks.

Unironically the entire patch could be rolled back, I wouldn't even cry over losing the relatively good (Normal mode is good, holy god the stat bloat in hard) story chapter or losing the pulls on the latest banners. it's that bad. In fact, it's SO bad that I'm not sure I'd feel comfortable spending money on it again unless they went further than rolling it back. the fact they even tried this, even if it got fully rolled back with an apology, dissuades investing in anything. Why would I spend money if half of the roster becomes outright unplayable for the primary content overnight? If interactions can get changed over a year after they occur *in the middle of a rerun banner*? if fights now take *sixty turns*? 

And how long until they do it again if it goes through, or try it in some different way if they do roll it mostly back?
